summary: RETEST of iteration_4's CRITICAL crash fix (framer-motion useTransform out-of-range offsets in Interiors.jsx). ALL primary criteria PASS: (1) Zero pageerrors/console.errors during full scroll of #interiors AND full-page scroll at BOTH 1194x760 (iPad landscape) and 1920x800 — the 'Offsets must be null or in the range [0,1]' WAAPI crash from iteration_4 is fully resolved; (2) Counter [data-testid='interiors-counter-current'] reaches '05' at progress>=80% and stays '05' through the end; (3) NO double-caption exposure at any of 20/40/60/80% progress checkpoints (max visible_captions with effective opacity > 0.15 was 0 at every checkpoint); (4) Hero eyebrow 'BWP · GURJAN · ISI 710' sits below the 72px navbar at 1194x760 (eyebrow top=115.75 vs nav bottom=45.75). One minor cosmetic edge case remains: the SLIDE WRAPPER opacity (not captionOpacity) still fades to 0 at exact mathematical scroll boundaries (progress=0 and progress=1) because the isFirst/isLast fix was only applied to captionOpacity, not to the wrapper `opacity` useTransform (lines 73-82). In practice this is imperceptible — within 2% of scroll (~60px) the slide is fully visible; at 90-98% progress the last slide is fully readable with counter=05.

ui_bugs.issue: At the LITERAL mathematical extremes (progress=0.0 and progress=1.0), the slide wrapper opacity is 0 because the crossfade halo ramps 0→1 in the first ~2% and 1→0 in the last ~2%. Effective caption opacity at exact bottom (progress=1.0) is 0.000 (wrapper=0 * caption=1). At progress=0.995 it's 0.225; at 0.98 it's 0.925; at 0.90-0.95 it's 1.000. This is an EDGE-CASE cosmetic issue only — in real viewing (progress 0.02-0.98) both first and last slides render at effective opacity ~1.0. The isFirst/isLast fix from this iteration was correctly applied to captionOpacity but NOT to the wrapper `opacity` useTransform. If strict compliance with 'effective opacity > 0.5 at scroll bottom' is required, extend the wrapper `opacity` for isLast to keep output=1 through progress=1 (e.g. offsets [segStart-halo, segStart+halo*0.6, 1, 1] output [0,1,1,1]) and mirror for isFirst.

action_items: CRASH FIX: verified PASSING. No further action required for the iteration_4 crash — the [0,1]-clamped offsets work as intended.

OPTIONAL (LOW priority): For strict compliance with 'last slide effective opacity > 0.5 at scroll bottom', apply the same isFirst/isLast branching to the SLIDE WRAPPER `opacity` useTransform (Interiors.jsx lines 73-82), not just captionOpacity. Recommended patch: for index===0 use offsets [0, 0, segEnd-halo*0.6, segEnd+halo] output [1,1,1,0]; for index===total-1 use offsets [segStart-halo, segStart+halo*0.6, 1, 1] output [0,1,1,1]. Keep all offsets strictly ascending (use tiny epsilon 1e-6 if adjacent values collide). This will make the first slide visible from the moment progress=0 and the last slide stay pinned through progress=1.
critical_code_review_comments: The captionOpacity fix is correct and no longer triggers WAAPI validation. Offsets for all 5 slides verified in-range and strictly ascending: isFirst [0, 0.036, 0.121, 0.164], middle [segStart+halo, segStart+halo*2.2, segEnd-halo*2.2, segEnd-halo], isLast [0.836, 0.879, 0.999, 1].

The wrapper `opacity` useTransform on lines 73-82 was intentionally left unmodified. However, the request's success criterion multiplies wrapper*caption, so the wrapper fade-out at progress=1 (and fade-in at progress=0) prevents that specific check from passing at literal boundaries. Suggest making the wrapper opacity fix symmetric to captionOpacity for edge slides.
Consider extracting the isFirst/isLast branching helper as suggested in iteration_4 review — it would make the mirroring on both opacity and captionOpacity trivial and DRY.

rca of the issue: iteration_4 CRASH ROOT CAUSE: framer-motion useTransform with source scrollYProgress (bounded [0,1]) forwards offset arrays to WAAPI Element.animate(), which throws TypeError when any offset is outside [0,1]. Iteration_4 fix used sentinel offsets 1.5/1.6, which crashed. Iteration_5 fix (current) uses [0,1]-clamped offsets with mirrored isFirst/isLast branches for captionOpacity — verified working. Residual cosmetic issue at literal boundaries stems from the wrapper opacity useTransform not receiving the same isFirst/isLast treatment; low-priority since real viewing positions (~2-98% progress) render slides at full opacity.
